doc.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 24, 2021 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Following his father to the Cuban radio orchestra
summary: His father, a violinist, took him to CMQ orchestra recordings, exposing him to many styles and charangas.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So did you start paying more attention to the percussion end of things with Cuban music?

Yes sir. My father was a violinist and he used to play for the Cuban National Radio Orchestra. So I used to go to the recordings were every day, Monday through Friday afternoons, and my father used to take me with him once I finished my day of schooling cause it was at that time just mornings. My father used to take me because my mom had passed away so he had no choice, taking me to his recordings. And that was the period when I was supposed to, on an every day basis [gap] music. The National Radio-TV Orchestra at that time there was a station called CMQ. The orchestra, they used to play © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

different styles of music because they used the recorded music for the radio and TV shows. And back in the days and to that period, the situation with American music and international music was not that heavy, ideologically speaking. I don’t know if that word is correct. So I used to listen to Cuban music, I used to listen — they used to record Brazilian music, Argentinean music, music from different countries. I was exposed to Cuban music since I was little, because my father used to play the violin at charangas — orchestra formations in Cuba that play Cuban genres like danzon, cha-cha-cha, so my father played with quite a few famous charangas and when I was little at my house my mother always had the radio on. Always. I’m coming from a very poor family where a guy, a musician, had to support a family by doing gigs and you know, and gigs used to get canceled and so forth and so on. So quite a few times I saw in my houses guys coming and taking the TV out of the house because my father couldn’t make the payments.
